Welcome to Bushfield School
Bushfield is a lively and busy place, where we aim to make the learning environment as exciting and challenging as possible. We’re pleased that you’re spending time finding out about the school and hope that our website is informative. At our heart, is a desire for our children to become skilful learners, team players, and, above all, leave us with fond memories and a sense of pride in themselves and their achievements; ready to take on the demands of secondary education and life beyond. If you have not yet come to visit us, I hope that we’ll meet in the near future. We look forward to offering you a warm welcome!
Mr S Springett-McHugh Mr S Weston
Executive Headteacher Associate Headteacher
Bushfield School is happy to provide, free of charge, paper copies of any information published on our website. Please make your request to Mr Rob Felce, School Business Manager, by calling 01908 314876 or emailing office@bushfieldschool.org
Viaduct Federation Vision Statement
The Viaduct Federation’s schools are at the heart of our communities. They are aspirational places where everyone shares enthusiasm and respect; where every individual child’s strengths are celebrated. We nurture and develop our pupils to become independent, adventurous learners who achieve highly through an inspiring and exciting curriculum.
Our staff are creative thinkers, reflective learners and proud of the Federation’s collective identity.
We are welcoming, open and honest; trusted and supported by the wider community to unlock the potential of all pupils for a life of integrity, ambition and happiness.
Curriculum Intent
At Bushfield, we have key curriculum drivers underpinning our ethos: imparting key knowledge (be a Skillful Learner); building individual character (Proud of who you are) and promoting a sense of social justice (Team Player). Everything we do in the school for our pupils builds to our inclusive motto of ‘be the best you can be’. We emphasise developing the whole child, providing a rich creative curriculum and ensuring a high standard of specialist education for all.

Our Governors
At Bushfield School, the governing body plays a vital role in ensuring the smooth and effective running of the school. Their core responsibilities include defining the school’s vision and strategic direction, overseeing the performance of the headteacher in relation to the school’s educational outcomes, and ensuring the proper and effective use of the school’s financial resources. Governors act with integrity and transparency, making decisions in the best interests of the school community. They also hold strategic oversight of safeguarding arrangements. Our governors are dedicated to continual self-development, contributing their time and expertise to help the school reflect and improve. We value diversity of thought, as it is essential to strong governance and the ongoing success of the school.
Could you join our governing board?
If you have skills in Finance; Strategic leadership; HR/People; Compliance; Sustainability; Diversity, Inclusion and Wellbeing; Data analysis; Digital & IT; Accountability governance or Early Years you would be a great fit for our team but we also welcome anyone who has a passion for making a difference and giving back to the community!
If you are interested in getting more involved with school life and becoming a school governor please email: chair@theviaductfederation.org or speak to the Headteacher.
Structure of Governing Board
Please follow the link below to see the structure of the Viaduct Federation of Schools Governing Board.
Appointment of Governors:
VFS Governing Board Constitution 2024-25
VFS – Committee Details 2024-2025
VFS Governing Board Constitution 2025-26
VFS Governing Board – Governor Declaration of Interests
Staff governors are elected by the staff.
Governor Meetings
Governor meetings are held each term across the academic year. We have two sub committees that meet outside of the full governing board; a Resources committee that focusses on the school’s budget and premises and a Curriculum committee that looks at the school’s provision and enrichment as well as the impact on children’s attainment and progress.

Governor minutes are public documents. If you are interested in joining our Governing Board or viewing the minutes, please make a request to the school office.

Information for Parents
Please scroll down for ‘Welcome to Bushfield’ videos
School Uniforms
At Bushfield we fully support school uniform and believe that it definitely contributes to team spirit, a positive attitude and gives the children a sense of pride. Our uniform is inexpensive and easy to obtain, either at Maisies in Wolverton or at MyClothing.com (previously Tesco). Follow the link to see our full uniform description.
Uniform Standard Policy – Bushfield
Wraparound Care
Premier Education Wraparound Care at Bushfield School
For more than 20 years, Premier Education has been delivering high-quality provision to primary schools nationwide, offering physical education, holiday camps, and a wide range of extra-curricular activities across both sporting and non-sporting subjects.
In 2016, we expanded our services to include wraparound care, bringing together our expertise in active, engaging provision with a convenient and seamless experience for parents. Our commitment to creating healthy, active, and enriching environments has made us the trusted choice for a growing number of schools.
Our Wraparound Provision
Running every day the school is open, from the end of the school day until 6:00 pm, our wraparound care offers a safe, fun, and nurturing environment that both children and parents can trust.
What Premier Education Wraparound Offers:
✅ Engaging Activities – With a new theme every week, children can enjoy a wide variety of fun, active, and stimulating experiences.
✅ Nutritious Meals & Snacks – A balanced menu designed to meet school food standards.
✅ Easy Online Booking – A straightforward system with instant confirmation, helping parents manage sessions effortlessly.
✅ Responsive Support – Our friendly team is available by phone or email, ensuring quick and helpful responses to any queries.
✅ Flexible Scheduling – Book up to two hours before on the same day, perfect for last-minute changes.
✅ Stress-Free Childcare – With our ‘Flexi Bookings’ option, parents can be in control of their bookings.
We’re thrilled to be supporting families at Bushfield School and look forward to welcoming your child to Premier Education Wraparound Care!
Life at Our Wraparound Care
Our wraparound care offers a true home-from-home environment, where children can relax, recharge, and feel at ease after a busy school day. Whether they’d like some quiet time or prefer to dive into exciting activities, there’s always something to enjoy in our warm and nurturing environment.
Every session is packed with fun and creativity. Children can lose themselves in imaginative play, build amazing structures with Lego, K’NEX, and building blocks, explore their artistic side at our creative stations, while our end-of-week movie night—complete with popcorn—offers the perfect opportunity to unwind with friends.
Alongside free play, we provide an enriching programme of adult-led activities designed to spark curiosity and broaden horizons. From edible crafts and construction challenges to team games and global themes, our sessions inspire children to learn about the wider world in engaging, stimulating ways.
More than just a wraparound club, we’re a community. Whether your child joins us every day or just now and then, they’ll always feel at home here.
Timings & Prices for Wraparound Care
We provide flexible wraparound care designed to fit your family’s routine, offering a safe, engaging, and fun space for your child before and after school. Sessions run every day the school is open, with different pick-up times to suit your schedule.
Session Options & Pricing:
All sessions include a wide variety of activities, from creative play to team games, plus a healthy snack in line with school food standards. Children staying until 6:00 pm will also enjoy a light tea, served between 5:00 pm and 5:15 pm.
How to Book Our Wraparound Care
Booking your child’s place at Premier Education Wraparound Care is quick and easy. Simply visit www.premier-education.com to get started.
New to Our Services?
If you’re booking with us for the first time, you will need to create an account. As part of the registration process, we will collect some important details—such as medical and dietary information—so we can provide the best care and support for your child.
Booking Your Sessions
Once your account is created, simply log in, choose your sessions, and confirm your booking in just a few clicks. You’ll receive an instant email confirmation, making it easy to keep track of your child’s schedule.
Important Information
To maintain safe staff-to-child ratios, all sessions run on a first-come, first-served basis. We encourage booking early to guarantee your child’s place.
If you have any questions or need help with bookings, our friendly support team is here to assist. We look forward to welcoming your child to our wraparound care!

Holiday Camps – Fun & Engaging Childcare When School’s Out!
At Premier Education, we understand that school holidays can be a juggling act for busy parents—that’s why we provide exciting, high-quality childcare when schools are closed. Our holiday camps, running at venues across Milton Keynes, offer a safe and vibrant environment where children can stay active, make friends, and take part in a wide variety of activities.
As the UK’s leading provider of sport and physical activity, we deliver expert coaching and fun, engaging games at every camp. But the experience doesn’t stop at sport—children also enjoy arts & crafts, outdoor adventures, team challenges, and themed enrichment activities that spark creativity and curiosity.
With flexible booking options and a programme designed to suit different ages and interests, our holiday camps give parents peace of mind while offering children days filled with fun, learning, and new experiences.
Extra Curricular Activities
​​Bushfield runs a wide variety of clubs throughout the week. A list of available clubs is sent out at the start of each term. While we cannot guarantee that a child will get into every club they choose, we try to accommodate their preferred choices. We also cannot guarantee that a child will get into a club for every day of the week however we try to accommodate as many children as possible. Please note that extra curricular clubs must be booked via Parentmail Forms.

Emergency Closure Procedure
Unfortunately, in very extreme circumstances we will deem it necessary to close the school. In the past during situations such as adverse weather conditions it has been very difficult for parents to ascertain whether to struggle to get their children into school.
To avoid this in the future Milton Keynes Council has a system which communicates school procedures not only to parents but also to the media. A website has been created for schools to log onto and close the school. It will then automatically update the local radio station and the Council Website.
If you think Bushfield may be closed, for example due to snow/flooding etc you can find out by visiting the Council’s Website: https://www.milton-keynes.gov.uk/closures?status=c/parent-info
Or you can listen to Heart FM Radio or BBC Three Counties Radio or visit their websites – www.heart.co.uk/ or www.bbc.co.uk/threecounties. We will continue to work with local radio stations to ensure that details of school closures are announced during their shows, for parents who do not have internet access at home.
Snow Letter – Jan 2026
Residential Visits
Residential visits can provide children with great opportunities to learn and grow, as well as to develop their independence. Bushfield offers a residential visit in each year group. They start simple in Year Three, with a one night sleepover at Safari MK. Year Four go on a three day geographical field study trip to Aylmerton in Norfolk. Year Five visit Whitemoor Lakes on a three day adventurous activity trip while Year Six visit Bournemouth for a celebratory residential, full of fun activities and visits by the seaside.
Homework
While there will be slight differences between year groups and classes, you can expect your child to receive weekly spelling words to learn. We also ask that children read a small amount on a daily basis. They will all have an appropriate reading book given to them by the school and are able to take out additional reading books through the library. Please could you encourage them to record their reading in their personal logs. The children will also be expected to practice their times tables on a daily basis. Occasionally your child may be set some additional maths or topic work to consolidate their learning from class.
Curriculum Newsletters
Each term your child’s year group will send out a Curriculum Newsletter. This will give you an overview of the topics and skills being studied in each subject along with relevant year group information such as up-coming trips or events. If you want to find out more about our curriculum for your child’s year group, please see the Curriculum Overview in the Key Information tab. Alternatively please contact the school to make arrangements to discuss our curriculum in more depth.

Information for New Parents/Carers
We are a junior school catering for children from Year 3 (aged 7) through to Year 6 (aged 11)
Bushfield is going from strength to strength – even Ofsted said so! Our school is ‘good’ with highly effective teaching and we are rightfully proud of what we have achieved.
We are thrilled to offer your children a four year educational journey, building on foundations of first school and help them to continue to learn and grow as they move through Key Stage 2 towards secondary school.

Working Partnerships
We make sure we have strong links with other schools and agencies to ensure the best support for our children. This includes close working partnership with the Local Council and their various departments such as Admissions, Attendance and the Inclusion and Assessment team. We also have strong links with our local cluster of schools (Radcliffe, Greenleys, Haversham, etc.) whom we meet regularly and discuss developments in teaching and learning and communal events that we can all attend.
We are also proactive in seeking specialist advice and support from private agencies where needed such as Play Therapists, Educational Psychologists and Pupil Referral Unit.
These links help form a supportive community of educationalists from whom we can share and draw support as needed
Vacancies
We are a very open and friendly staff team. There is a strong commitment from everyone at the school to provide the best environment for the children to learn in – whether that’s in the classroom, at break and lunch times or down to the cleanliness of the school. Any vacancies to join the team are posted here.

School Timetable
The school opens at 8:35am and the children come straight into the building and to their classrooms. Children arriving after 8:45am should go to the school office and sign in as a late arrival.
Morning break is at 10:45 – 11:00amLunchtime is between 12:00 – 13:00
The school day ends at 15:15
After school clubs* finish at 16:15
* Please note that afterschool clubs do not run in the first and last week of each term.
** This equates to 32.5 hours a week.
Office Hours
The school office is open from 8am to 4.45pm. You can leave a message on the answer machine if you can only contact us outside of these times.
Our Staff
Bushfield has a strong staff team of dedicated people who all work closely together to deliver the best for the children. Please follow the link below to see the full staff list.
Breakfast Club
Breakfast club is an informal morning drop in session run by the school where there is no need to book or sign up in advance. It opens at 7:45am – 08:45am in the main school hall and offers a variety of foods both hot and cold. The session costs a flat rate of £2.00 (payable through parent mail either daily or a week at a time). The children also have the opportunity to take part in early morning games and play as part of the session. Please contact the school office if you have any further questions.
